problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x+2y,\,y(1)=1
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method with step size $Δx=\frac{1}{4}.$ Fill in the empty box in the column for $Δy$ in the table below using this method. Do not round the answer.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ |  |  | {{field-1}} |
worked_solution:
First, because the initial condition is $y(1)=1,$ we fill $y=1$ into the table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $$ | $$ |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x+2y \\  & =1+2(1) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $3$ | $$ |

Finally, we compute $Δy$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =3(\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $3$ | $\frac{3}{4}$ |
